title: Rav Shemaya II
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was a disciple of Rava. In [Eruvin 40a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.40a.7-8), Rava bar Tachlifa said to Ravina—Rav Shemaya challenged it—they went and asked Rava, who ruled in accordance with Rav Shemaya. In [Pesachim 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.25a.8-9) he raised a difficulty that Rava resolved, and in [Nazir 52a](https://www.sefaria.org/Nazir.52a.2-3) he addresses a query of Rava. In [Pesachim 49a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.49a.20) he is mentioned after Rav Pappa and says, “And they call him the son of one who folds his garment and lies down.”[^1] In [Pesachim 23a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.23a.8) he says, “It is different there, for Scripture says ‘your harvest,’” etc.[^2]

notes.text: בר מך רבע is an insulting nickname. Rashi on Pesachim 49a:20 explains it as the son of someone who folds his garment beneath him and lies down to sleep drunk; קרו ליה refers to the son. The fuller passage places Rav Pappa immediately before Rav Shemaya.

א״ק abbreviates אמר קרא, “Scripture says.” The Eruvin passage reads אזלו שיילוה לרבא, “they went and asked Rava,” corresponding to the accepted transcription’s אולו שילו. The heading’s ב) distinguishes this notice as II. The description of Shemaya as Rava’s disciple is Hyman’s.
